prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map captures the continuous ground plane of the lawn sloping away from the camera wearer (0.5 m to over 15 m), flanked by a brick building wall on the left (1–3 m) and parked cars in the distant upper right (10–20 m). In the foreground within arm's reach (0.3–1.2 m), it clearly separates a translucent plastic tub on the left, a water bottle ~0.5 m to its right (frames 1–2), a towel with takeout containers and a yellow chip bag directly below the camera wearer (frames 2–4), and the camera wearer's own legs/hands at the bottom right (~0.3–0.5 m). Across frames 2 to 5, a young child inside the tub (~0.8–1.2 m away) rises and leans forward and downward toward the towel to within ~0.5–0.8 m of the camera wearer, while the camera tilts down in frames 3–4 and back up in frame 5 as the child settles lower into the tub. Compared to RGB, the depth map makes the 3D surface geometry of the translucent tub walls and the distance relief between the child's leaning torso and the tub behind them much clearer. However, the map is unreliable on transparent and refractive surfaces, rendering the lower half of the water bottle artificially bright (nearer) than its top and flattening the water inside the tub against the tub's back wall.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map isolates discrete foreground and background entities, locating distant cars (~10–20 m away in the upper right in frames 1, 4, and 5), the camera wearer's lower legs/hands at the bottom right (~0.3–0.6 m), a water bottle on the right in frame 2 (~0.9 m), and the child in the centre-left foreground (~0.6–1.0 m) from frame 3 onward. It shows the child's upper body emerging above and in front of the tub in frames 3–5, leaning down to the left so their right hand contacts a small object (~0.7 m away, ~0.4 m left of the yellow bag) before retracting slightly rightward into the tub by frame 5. The masks highlight silhouettes and boundary overlaps—such as the child's torso occluding the tub rim and the camera wearer's hand overlapping the bottom edge in frame 3—that blend into the busy grass and towel textures in the RGB frames. However, the map is highly unreliable in class labels and recall: it completely misses the plastic tub in all frames, the water bottle in frames 1 and 5, and the child's arm in frame 2, while misclassifying the brick wall as a 'bench', the child as a 'dog' (frame 3), the yellow snack bag as a 'cake', and the small cup/object by the child's hand as a 'sports ball'.
descriptions.pose: The pose map tracks the 2D skeletal keypoints of the child in the tub (~0.6–1.0 m in front of the camera wearer), capturing how they lean forward out of the tub from frame 3 to frame 5 while facing toward and slightly down to the left of the camera wearer without looking directly into the lens. In frames 3 and 4, the yellow torso quadrilateral and limb segments show the child's right arm extending straight down into the bottom-left foreground within reach of the ground beside the towel, while the left arm bends backward with its magenta hand gripping the tub's rim ~0.4 m to the right; by frame 5, the child drops lower so the torso and right hand are occluded below the bottom frame edge. The skeleton and dense facial/hand keypoints clarify exact joint articulations, shoulder tilt, head orientation, and finger placement on the translucent tub edge that are blurred and motion-degraded in the RGB image. However, the pose estimator is unreliable when body parts are partially out of view, misinterpreting the camera wearer's foot/leg on the far right of frame 2 (~0.6 m away) as a tiny inverted head-and-torso skeleton and failing to detect the camera wearer's visible hand in frame 3 or the child's arm in frame 2.
